target_moa.text: Lesinurad is a URAT1 inhibitor that reduces serum uric acid by inhibiting uric acid reabsorption transporters URAT1 and OAT4 on the apical surface of renal tubular cells, increasing renal uric acid excretion

citations.quote: Lesinurad reduces serum uric acid levels by inhibiting the function of transporter proteins involved in uric acid reabsorption in the kidney. Lesinurad inhibited the function of two apical transporters responsible for uric acid reabsorption, uric acid transporter 1 (URAT1) and organic anion transporter 4 (OAT4), with IC50 values of 7.3 and 3.7 \muM, respectively.
ZURAMPIC causes an increase in renal uric acid excretion, which may lead to renal events including transient increases in serum creatinine, renal-related adverse reactions, and kidney stones.

ZURAMPIC (lesinurad) is a URAT1 inhibitor. Lesinurad has the following chemical name: 2-((5-bromo-4-(4-cyclopropylnaphthalen-1-yl)-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio)acetic acid. The molecular formula is C_{17}H_{14}BrN_3O_2S and the molecular weight is 404.28. The structural formula is:

key_safety.text: Most serious risk is renal: in combination with XOI, renal failure reported in 1.2% (200 mg) vs 2.1% (placebo) and blood creatinine increased 4.3% (200 mg) vs 2.3% (placebo); monotherapy at 400 mg caused renal failure 9.3% and serum creatinine elevations >=1.5-fold in 24.3%. Most common adverse reactions with 200 mg: headache 5.3%, influenza 5.1%, gastroesophageal reflux disease 2.7%.

requirement.text: Study 3014-1: A randomized, controlled clinical trial to evaluate the safety of lesinurad 200 mg on background XOI with respect to renal function and renal adverse events, enriched with moderate renal impairment patients, minimum 2-year treatment duration, including adjudicated assessment of cardiovascular safety

citations.quote: A randomized, controlled, clinical trial to evaluate the safety of lesinurad 200mg on a background of concomitant xanthine oxidase inhibitor, with respect to renal function and renal adverse events, in gout patients who have not achieved target serum uric acid with a xanthine oxidase inhibitor alone. Enrollment should be enriched with patients with moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance 30 to 60 mL/min). The minimum treatment duration should be 2 years. The trial must also include an assessment of cardiovascular (CV) safety based on an independent adjudication of prospectively defined and collected CV events.
